technical_and_design_decisions: The increment targets a Spring XD-style distributed runtime (streams, modules, containers, message bus) built on Spring Integration, Spring AMQP, and Spring Boot, as implied by the user stories.

U1: Implement the alternative DLQ as a configurable per-bus/per-module dead-letter destination; failed messages are republished with added headers carrying the exception class, message, and the stack trace serialized as a String header to guarantee transport safety.

U2: Implement the database-change (CDC) source as an out-of-the-box stream module using incremental polling (timestamp/version columns and change tables) via a Spring Integration JDBC inbound adapter, emitting canonical JSON change events onto the bus so any sink (broker, Hadoop, DB) can consume them.

U3: Support RabbitMQ HA/FT by accepting a list of cluster node addresses (host:port) in the connection factory configuration, leveraging spring-amqp's multi-address failover; upstream the change to spring-amqp if required.

U5: Colocation is achieved by deploying all modules of a stream into a single container JVM while preserving module classloader isolation; automatic failover uses leader election built on the existing ZooKeeper/Curator infrastructure already used by the runtime.
U8: Align all managed dependency versions with the Spring Boot 1.2.3 BOM using dependency-management overrides, then resolve incompatibilities iteratively until the full build and test suite pass.

The framework overview in the specification is descriptive only; the concrete versions named in the stories (Boot 1.2.3, Gemfire 8.1, SI GA, SI Kafka) define the target stack, on the project's existing JDK baseline (Java 8).
assumptions: All estimates are ideal engineering workdays (8 hours) for one senior developer performing all work, and exclude elapsed-time waits (e.g., external release timelines for Gemfire 8.1, Spring Data Gosling, SI milestones).
The external dependencies referenced in the stories (Gemfire 8.1, Spring Data Gosling GA, SI GA, SI Kafka release, Spring Boot 1.2.3) are available when work begins.
An existing codebase, build system, CI pipeline, and integration test environments (RabbitMQ cluster, databases, ZooKeeper, Gemfire) are available; no infrastructure provisioning effort is included.

Effort covers analysis, design, implementation, unit and integration testing, and documentation of the increment; production deployment, operations, project management, and release process overhead are excluded.

For U2, a polling-based CDC approach is assumed (no licensing or integration of a third-party log-based CDC product); supported databases are limited to those already supported by the platform's JDBC modules.
Defects found during increment-level integration testing are fixed within the hardening activity; no major architectural rework is triggered by the dependency upgrades.
Since a single developer performs all work, code review is performed as structured self-review within the hardening activity.
